name: J. David Joyner

career.title: Executive Vice President, Sales and Account Services
Executive Vice President, Sales and Marketing
Executive Vice President and President, CVS Caremark

background_rationale: Built his career in health-benefit sales and account management, rising from Aetna benefit representative and Caremark regional sales manager to run sales and marketing and then the Caremark PBM before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: CVS announced Aetna would stop offering individual ACA exchange plans in 2026, affecting about 1 million members, with Joyner saying there was no near- or long-term pathway for Aetna to materially improve its position.
At an investor day, CVS laid out a four-pillar strategy, launched an AI-based 'Engagement as a Service' platform and set a mid-teens adjusted EPS growth target through 2028.
Joyner became Chair of the Board in addition to CEO, succeeding executive chair Roger Farah, after the board decided to combine the two roles.
CVS reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $106.1 billion, up 7.3% year over year, and raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.90-$8.10.

personal_story.hook: David Joyner began as an Aetna benefits representative; today he runs CVS Health, which owns Aetna.
personal_story.summary: Joyner graduated from Texas Tech University in 1986 with a finance degree and started his career at Aetna as an employee benefit representative. He moved to Caremark Prescription Services as a regional sales manager and spent decades in pharmacy-benefit sales, rising to run sales and account services for CVS Caremark. He left CVS around the end of 2019 and advised private equity-backed healthcare companies, then returned in 2023 to lead Caremark. In October 2024 he was named CEO of CVS Health, and in January 2026 he also became its chair.
